claim: Player starts are marker sprites: type 1 for single player and co-op, type 2 for Bloodbath, data1 the player's number; type 1 number 0 is where a game alone starts. The engine reads them into start zones at load and deletes them. The campaign maps carry eight type-1 markers (one map nine) and seven to nine type-2 (pictures 2522-2529). The map header's start is only a fallback and is not where the game starts: in 37 of 43 campaign maps it lies in another sector than the marker. Pick number 0, not the first marker by index: in 12 maps the first is another number.
evidence: NBlood/source/blood/src/warp.cpp:61-70 (warpInit) kMarkerSPStart -> gStartZone[data1] for nGameType <= coop, DeleteSprite; warp.cpp:72-80 kMarkerMPStart for Bloodbath

knowledge/blood/findings/probes/audit2_player_starts.py (2026-11-26): eight type-1 markers in 42 maps and nine in one; type-2 seven in 4, eight in 36, nine in 3; header sector differs from type 1 number 0 in 37; first type-1 marker by index is not number 0 in 12 maps
NBlood/source/blood/src/blood.cpp:724-731 (StartLevel): the header start fills gStartZone first and is only the fallback
use: Give every map both eights; stand number 0 of type 1 exactly where the player should begin.
